# Initialization
units metal
atom_style full
boundary p p p

# Read molten structure
read_data /structures/melt/SiO2/melt.dat

# Define potential
pair_style tersoff
pair_coeff * * /potentials/TERSOFF/2007_SiO.tersoff Si O

# Neighbor settings
neighbor 2.0 bin
neigh_modify every 1 delay 0 check yes

# Timestep
timestep 0.001

# Compute temperature and pressure
compute myTemp all temp
compute myPress all pressure myTemp

# NPT quenching from 5000K to 1500K at 3.5 K/ps
# Total time: (5000-1500)/3.5 = 1000 ps = 1,000,000 steps
# Output every 1000 steps = 1 ps intervals

fix 1 all npt temp 5000 1500 $(100.0*dt) iso 0.0 0.0 $(1000.0*dt)

# Thermo output every 1000 steps (1 ps)
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp press density vol pe ke etotal

# Run quenching simulation
run 1000000

# Write final structure

temp = df['Temp'].values
density = df['Density'].values

# Sort by temperature (descending, from high to low)
sort_idx = np.argsort(temp)[::-1]
temp_sorted = temp[sort_idx]
density_sorted = density[sort_idx]

print(f"Density range: {density_sorted.min():.4f} - {density_sorted.max():.4f} g/cm³")
print(f"Number of data points: {len(temp_sorted)}")

# Method: Find Tg by detecting change in slope using sliding window linear regression
# We'll fit two lines: one for high T (liquid) and one for low T (glass)
# and find their intersection

# Try different split points and find the one with best fit
best_tg = None
best_r2_sum = -np.inf

# Only consider middle 60% of temperature range for potential Tg
temp_min = temp_sorted.min()
temp_max = temp_sorted.max()
temp_range = temp_max - temp_min
search_min = temp_min + 0.2 * temp_range
search_max = temp_max - 0.2 * temp_range

for i in range(len(temp_sorted)):
    t_split = temp_sorted[i]
    
    # Skip if outside search range
    if t_split < search_min or t_split > search_max:
        continue
    
    # Split data into high-T (liquid) and low-T (glass) regions
    high_t_mask = temp_sorted >= t_split
    low_t_mask = temp_sorted < t_split
    
    # Need at least 20 points in each region for good fit
    if np.sum(high_t_mask) < 20 or np.sum(low_t_mask) < 20:
        continue
    
    # Fit linear regression for each region
    high_t_temp = temp_sorted[high_t_mask]
    high_t_density = density_sorted[high_t_mask]
    low_t_temp = temp_sorted[low_t_mask]
    low_t_density = density_sorted[low_t_mask]
    
    # Linear fit for high temperature (liquid)
    slope_high, intercept_high, r_high, _, _ = stats.linregress(high_t_temp, high_t_density)
    
    # Linear fit for low temperature (glass)
    slope_low, intercept_low, r_low, _, _ = stats.linregress(low_t_temp, low_t_density)
    
    # Calculate R² for both fits
    r2_high = r_high ** 2
    r2_low = r_low ** 2
    r2_sum = r2_high + r2_low
    
    # We want both fits to be good (high R²) and slopes to be different
    slope_diff = abs(slope_high - slope_low)
    
    # Update best Tg if this split gives better fits
    if r2_sum > best_r2_sum and slope_diff > 0.0001:
        best_r2_sum = r2_sum
        best_tg = t_split
        best_high_slope = slope_high
        best_high_intercept = intercept_high
        best_low_slope = slope_low
        best_low_intercept = intercept_low
        best_r2_high = r2_high
        best_r2_low = r2_low

print(f"\nGlass Transition Temperature (Tg): {best_tg:.2f} K")
print(f"High-T slope: {best_high_slope:.6f} g/cm³/K (R² = {best_r2_high:.4f})")
print(f"Low-T slope: {best_low_slope:.6f} g/cm³/K (R² = {best_r2_low:.4f})")
print(f"Slope ratio: {abs(best_low_slope/best_high_slope):.2f}")

# Calculate intersection point of the two lines for more precise Tg
if best_high_slope != best_low_slope:
    tg_intersection = (best_low_intercept - best_high_intercept) / (best_high_slope - best_low_slope)
    print(f"Tg from line intersection: {tg_intersection:.2f} K")

low_t_mask = temp_sorted < best_tg

low_t_fit = best_low_slope * temp_sorted[low_t_mask] + best_low_intercept

plt.plot(temp_sorted[low_t_mask], low_t_fit, 'b-', linewidth=2, label=f'Glass (slope={best_low_slope:.6f})')
plt.axvline(final_tg, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, label=f'Tg = {final_tg:.2f} K')

plt.xlabel('Temperature (K)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Density (g/cm³)', fontsize=12)
plt.title('SiO2 Quenching: Density vs Temperature', fontsize=14)
plt.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.grid(true, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('density_vs_temp.png', dpi=150)
print(f"\nPlot saved as density_vs_temp.png")

# Save final Tg value
with open('tg_value.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"{final_tg:.2f}")

print(f"\nFinal Tg value saved to tg_value.txt: {final_tg:.2f} K")

    """Fit two linear segments and return total residual"""
    if breakpoint_idx < 50 or breakpoint_idx > len(temp) - 50:

        res_low = np.sum((density_low - np.polyval(p_low, temp_low))**2)
